testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to handle dangerous situations.
Turn your head around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to handle dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: Watch the road for hazards. Think ahead about what you will do if a hazard becomes an emergency.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you stop on the side of the road. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: Antifreeze helps your engine work properly:
questions.explanation: Keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system at all times. Despite its name, antifreeze is helpful even in hot weather.

questions.question: At speeds below 40 mph, you should stay back at least ____ for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length.
questions.explanation: Below 40 mph, allow one second of distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle. At higher speeds, use the same formula and add one more second. Larger vehicles need more space to stop.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Helps you stay awake on long trips.

questions.explanation: Rough acceleration damages your engine. Speed up slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: A maximum safe speed sign means:

options.text: You can drive faster if you choose to.
Only heavy vehicles over 26,000 pounds must follow it.
No vehicle should drive faster than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: No vehicle should drive faster than the posted speed.
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed shown on a maximum safe speed sign.

questions.question: When driving downhill, brake until your speed is:
questions.explanation: Brake until your vehicle slows to 5 mph below your safe speed, then release the brake. Repeat as needed going downhill.

questions.question: A pre-trip vehicle inspection:

options.text: Is not needed if you drive the vehicle often.
Is not needed for trips under 100 miles.
Only a mechanic can do it.

questions.explanation: State and federal law require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving.

questions.question: If your coolant temperature gauge goes too high, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check what is wrong.
questions.explanation: Stop driving right away if the coolant temperature is too high. There may be a serious problem that could cause engine failure or a fire.

questions.question: Looking ahead of your vehicle while driving is:

options.text: Not helpful because you cannot control things far ahead.

questions.explanation: Look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and react safely.

questions.question: Why should your mirrors show the road behind you and part of your vehicle?

options.text: Seeing only the road in mirrors would make the driver carsick.
Seeing part of your vehicle in the mirrors helps you judge distances to other vehicles.
It is illegal to show only the road in the mirrors.
You need to see reflections of surrounding vehicles on the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Seeing part of your vehicle in the mirrors helps you judge distances to other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Part of your vehicle should be visible in your mirrors. This gives you a reference point to judge how close other drivers and objects are to your vehicle.

questions.question: When traction is poor, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always the best practice.
So you do not lose control of your vehicle.
So you do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So you do not lose control of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Speeding up too quickly on slippery roads can cause you to lose control. When traction is poor, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Which sign shows that a driver is drowsy?

options.text: Eyes going out of focus by themselves

questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include eyes closing or blurring on their own, difficulty holding your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: Drivers talking to passengers should be viewed as:
questions.explanation: Talking to passengers takes attention away from driving. Be careful around drivers who are talking to passengers in their vehicle.

questions.question: Which of the following is not tie-down equipment?
questions.explanation: Use the correct tie-down equipment to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer. Ropes, straps, and chains are proper tie-down equipment.

questions.question: When starting a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn on and then shut off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on and then shut off quickly.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, warning lights and buzzers should turn on briefly, then turn off.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, the air compressor governor will:

options.text: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
Start pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping air when tanks reach about 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: If an approaching vehicle has high beam headlights on, you should:

options.text: Flash your high beams to tell the driver to turn them off.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights toward the right edge of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the lights.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing during a driving test, you should:

options.text: Pass a slow vehicle on the tracks if needed.
Get out of the vehicle to check for trains.
Not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During a driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a refrigerated truck:

options.text: Is good practice for inexperienced drivers.

questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable cargo. It has a high center of gravity and the swinging meat can affect how you control the vehicle. Only skilled drivers should transport this load.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a single vehicle with air brakes during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A single vehicle with air brakes must not lose more than 3 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Which statement about the pre-trip vehicle inspection test is correct?

options.text: You do not have to identify the ABS.
You do not have to check windshield wipers.
You only need to check shock absorbers on one axle.
You must check the steering box for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must check the steering box for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the external pre-trip inspection, you must check that the steering box is properly mounted and is not leaking.

questions.question: What may the air in air storage tanks contain?
questions.explanation: Air entering storage tanks in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. These materials can damage the braking system, so tanks have drains to remove them.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do with your turn signal?

options.text: Only use it if another vehicle is close to you

questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you are signaling.

questions.question: Which reason may cause an applicant to be denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
Having a speeding conviction in the past three years
Not answering every question correctly on the written hazardous materials test
Not passing the written hazardous materials test on the first try

questions.correctAnswerText: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you give up U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are wanted or convicted of certain felonies, are judged mentally defective, are committed to a mental institution, or are deemed a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration.

questions.question: What happens if one-fourth of the leaves in a leaf spring are missing during inspection?

options.text: The driver can continue driving at reduced speeds
The vehicle must be taken out of service until repaired
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is still there

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until repaired
questions.explanation: Check for broken or missing leaves in leaf springs during suspension inspection. This is dangerous. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing from any leaf spring, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: How should your mirrors be adjusted before a trip?

options.text: Your vehicle should not be visible in any mirror
Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors
More than half of each mirror should show your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Part of your vehicle should be visible in the mirrors
questions.explanation: When properly adjusted, your mirrors should show some part of your vehicle. Seeing your own vehicle in your mirrors helps you judge the position of other objects.

questions.question: What emergency equipment must a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher is only needed if carrying hazardous materials
A fire extinguisher is only needed when traveling through remote areas
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three red reflective triangles or flares, and at least one charged and rated fire extinguisher.

questions.question: How should the steering wheel be held while driving?

options.text: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
With both hands at the bottom of the wheel
With both hands at the top of the wheel

questions.correctAnswerText: With both hands on opposite sides of the wheel
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands placed on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Prevent the front tires from skidding
Prevent the front tires from overheating
Remove uncertainty when applying the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the front tires from skidding
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have front brake limiting valves meant to reduce the risk of front wheels skidding. However, research showed these devices are not needed, so they should be left in the normal position.

questions.question: What shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells you how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to reach 85 to 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems. This takes about 45 seconds.

questions.question: When entering a foggy area, you should:

options.text: Stop on the side of the roadway.

questions.explanation: Always slow down when entering fog. Use low beam headlights. Do not pass other vehicles or stop on the side of the road. Avoid driving in fog if possible.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating your large vehicle, do all of the following except:
questions.explanation: If being tailgated, increase your following distance and slow down gradually. Do not speed up. The other driver will just tailgate you at a higher speed. Do not flash your brake lights.

questions.question: When construction workers are near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait to proceed until the construction is complete.

questions.explanation: In construction zones, follow posted speed limits. Slow down even more when workers are near the roadway.

questions.question: Both systems in a dual air brake system share:
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the air compressor fails, neither system will work.

questions.question: Braking mechanisms are located inside:
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels on the axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are inside the brake drum.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Press on and finish the trip.
Drive faster to reach your destination more quickly.
Safely leave the road and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely leave the road and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, stop and sleep. Tired drivers cause many fatal accidents. Do not try to finish your trip while fatigued.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see hazards in the dark.

questions.question: In hot weather, spots on the pavement where tar is bleeding:

options.text: Offer the same amount of traction as the rest of the roadway.
Offer more traction than the rest of the roadway.

questions.explanation: In hot weather, tar in the road rises to the surface. These spots are very slippery, so watch for them.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check how tight the nuts are if you see rust in this area.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control your vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, what should you do?

options.text: Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: During the driving skills test, you may need to enter an expressway. Always check traffic first, use your turn signal, and merge smoothly into the correct lane.

questions.question: What is true about using turn signals?

options.text: It is best to hide your intentions from others.
Use turn signals only when other vehicles are nearby.
Do not use turn signals in construction zones.
Always use turn signals to warn others of your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to warn others of your plans.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Use your turn signal before turning or changing lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: When should service brakes be tested?
questions.explanation: Always test your service brakes before you drive. Testing them before a trip helps you find problems before you need to stop on the road.

questions.question: What should you check on a cargo lift?

options.text: That it is the correct color.

questions.explanation: During your vehicle inspection, check the cargo lift for leaks, damage, or missing parts. The lift must be fully closed and locked in place.

questions.question: What is axle weight?

options.text: The weight that one axle puts on the ground.
The weight of the axle itself.
The maximum weight an axle can hold.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight that one axle puts on the ground.
questions.explanation: Axle weight is the weight that one axle or set of axles puts on the ground.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap, what should you check?

options.text: That the locking jaws are open.
That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
That the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Make sure the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed tightly around the kingpin shaft, not just around the kingpin head.

questions.question: If spring brakes activate while carrying a heavy load, stopping will:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. When air pressure is low and spring brakes activate, your vehicle needs more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection after starting the vehicle, how should the coolant temperature change?
questions.explanation: After you start your vehicle, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually increase to the normal operating range.
